'''''Panicum dichotomiflorum''''', known by the common names '''fall panicgrass''', '''autumn millet''' (Britain and Ireland),<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> and '''fall panicum'''<ref>{{cite book|author=Mary E. Barkworth |author2=Laurel K. Anderton |author3=Kathleen M. Capel |author4=Sandy Long |author5=Michael B. Piep |title=Manual of Grasses for North America|publisher=University Press of Colorado|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BNC9AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT1077|year=2007|isbn=978-0-87421-686-8}}</ref> is a species of [[Poaceae]] "true grass". It is native to much of the eastern United States and parts of Canada, and it can be found in the [[Western United States]] through [[California]]. It may be an [[introduced species]] in some western climates.<ref>[http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Panicum_dichotomiflorum&type=treatment Grass Manual Treatment] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611161418/http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Panicum_dichotomiflorum&type=treatment |date=2011-06-11 }}</ref>

==Description==
''Panicum dichotomiflorum'' is an annual [[grass]] growing decumbent or erect to a maximum height near one meter-3 feet. It can be distinguished from its relative, [[Panicum capillare|''Panicum capillare'' - Witchgrass]] by its hairless leaves.<ref>[http://www.ipm.ucdavis.edu/PMG/WEEDS/fall_panicum.html UC Davis IPM]</ref> The [[inflorescence]] is a large open [[panicle]] up to 20 centimeters long and fanning out to a width of 16 centimeters.

== Ecology ==

=== Habitat ===
''P. dichotomiflorum'' can be found in moist habitats including floodplain, streams, disturbed areas and [[chaparral]] [[habitat]]s.<ref>Bostick, P. E. (1971). "Vascular Plants of Panola Mountain, Georgia " Castanea 46(3): 194-209.</ref> It requires full sun.

=== Phenology ===
This species flowers from mid-summer through the fall.<ref>Weakley, A.S. 2015. Flora of the southern and mid-atlantic states. Working Draft of 21 May 2015. University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, North Carolina.</ref>
